factor.description: Determine whether governance proposal execution can route proposal-supplied calls or delegatecalls to arbitrary targets without an allowlist, distinguishing executor-storage delegatecall risk from ordinary external call risk and from manual/off-chain execution.

factor.name: delegatecall/call in proposal execution without allowlist
factor.scoring_methodology:
**What this measures**
This factor evaluates the proposal execution path behind protocol governance. The highest-risk pattern is executor-context `delegatecall` to proposal-supplied code or target addresses without an on-chain allowlist, because proposal code can execute against the executor's own storage and authority. Ordinary external `call` to proposal-supplied targets remains governance-power risk, but it is not equivalent to arbitrary code execution in executor storage.

**Green / Yellow / Red / Gray**
Green is assigned when there is no automated on-chain proposal executor, execution is manual signer action after off-chain governance, proposal execution is limited to typed/predefined actions, or callable targets are strictly allowlisted. Fixed internal delegatecall to immutable protocol extensions is also green when the proposal cannot choose the delegatecall target. Yellow is assigned when governance can execute proposal-supplied external `call` targets/calldata without a strict allowlist, but the path does not delegate into executor storage and meaningful safeguards such as timelocks, cancellation powers, quorum, or multisig implementation reduce exploitability. Red is assigned when proposal execution permits unrestricted proposal-supplied `delegatecall`, or an equivalent executor-context arbitrary execution path, without a strict allowlist. Gray is reserved for cases where the executor path, deployed source, or current governance implementation cannot be verified well enough to determine the execution semantics.

**Common gray cases**
Gray should be used for unverified or ambiguous executor paths, not merely because governance execution is manual or off-chain. Manual execution after Snapshot/forum voting is a green outcome when no automated proposal executor accepts arbitrary proposal calldata.

**Critical factor**
A red assessment remains critical because unrestricted executor-context arbitrary execution can convert a passed proposal into a full governance takeover primitive.

scored_protocols.evidence_summary: [★] No governance executor, no proposal payload mechanism, no delegatecall in proposal path. Not applicable by construction.

Solana programs do not use delegatecall. No on-chain proposal execution path with arbitrary call/delegatecall. Squads executes BPF upgrade transactions via BPFLoaderUpgradeable, not arbitrary proposal payloads with target allowlists. EVM-specific attack vector does not apply.

pDAO proposal execution targets a single hardcoded contract: getContractAddress('rocketDAOProtocolProposals'). This is an effective target allowlist of one permitted contract. No user-supplied delegatecall target. RocketDAOProtocolProposals contract exposes only governance settings, treasury, and Security Council management functions — all restricted by onlyExecutingContracts() modifier.
No on-chain Governor or proposal executor. Governance is Snapshot off-chain; execution is manual multisig. No delegatecall-in-proposal path exists.

scored_protocols.evidence_detail: Governor Bravo accepts proposal-supplied target/value/signature/calldata arrays and dispatches them to a route-specific timelock. Timelock.executeTransaction uses target.call.value(value)(callData) without an allowlist. Venus documents a Critical VIP as six hours of voting plus a one-hour timelock; the Governor’s guardian can cancel before execution and vote weight is checkpointed. The unrestricted call path combined with the seven-hour Critical route meets the v1.7 red calibration’s short-review-window condition. This does not rely on the unrelated 2025 social-engineering incident as a governance-executor near miss.
scored_protocols.evidence_summary: Governor proposals supply arbitrary targets and calldata to Timelock.call without an allowlist; a Critical VIP can complete six hours of voting plus a one-hour timelock. The short execution window makes this unrestricted executor path red under v1.7.
